A warm, home-like place where little hearts grow & bright futures blossom.

Bright Saplings is a licensed in-home daycare in Bothell for toddlers and preschoolers, 18 months to 5 years. Nurturing today, inspiring tomorrow.

We keep our groups small on purpose. It means every child is known by name, every parent gets a real conversation at pickup, and the day can bend around a child who needs a little longer with something.

What makes us special

  • A warm, home-like environment

    Where children feel safe, loved and supported. A second home, not an institution.

  • Play-based learning

    Building confidence, curiosity and a genuine love for learning, not worksheets.

  • Nutritious meals and snacks

    Cooked here every morning by a trained baker, with allergies taken seriously.

  • Small class sizes

    Personalized care and meaningful attention, every day, for every child.

  • Social-emotional development

    Helping children grow kind, confident and independent. That is the part that lasts.

  • Daily outdoor play

    Time outside every day it's safe, to support active, healthy little bodies.

Our story

It started with her own two.

Founder Pooja Agarwal Baker, mother of two,
and the reason this house is loud

Pooja Agarwal came here from India with her husband and two small children: a daughter, and a son a few years behind her. Everything Bright Saplings is now started in that house, long before it had a name.

Starting over

A new country is a quiet place at first. There is a school run to work out, a house that doesn't smell like home yet, and a very small person holding your hand who is also working it all out.

So she baked

It was the thing that made the house feel like hers. Then neighbors started asking, and friends of neighbors after that.

Sugar n Flakes Bakery & Cafe

The asking turned into a store. Years of it: early mornings, real ingredients, and learning exactly how much a small person will actually eat.

And then the children

What she hadn't planned for was who a warm room fills up with. Parents, and their children, and the slow realization that the part of the day she looked forward to was the small people at the table, not the counter.

A child should be somewhere they are known by name, fed properly, and allowed to take their time. That is the whole idea.

Bright Saplings

Bright Saplings is the same person, the same kitchen and the same standards, in a house built around children rather than a counter. Her daughter and son are older now, and both still get roped in when there's baking to do.

Come and meet her

Toddlers and preschoolers, under one roof.

Children move up when they're ready, not on a birthday, and they share the same table, the same yard and the same grown-ups the whole way through.

Food

Before this was a daycare,
it was a bakery.

Every meal and every snack is cooked here, in this kitchen, by someone who did it professionally for years. That is not a marketing line. It is just what happened to be true when we opened.

Sugar n Flakes Bakery & Cafe

The same hands, the same oven.

Pooja ran Sugar n Flakes Bakery & Cafe before Bright Saplings existed. Scratch cooking, real ingredients, portioning for small appetites, and a genuinely obsessive approach to what goes into a bowl. All of it came with her into this kitchen and never left.

It means a child here eats food that was made this morning by a person who knows their name, not something reheated out of a catering box.

Read how the journey started

  • Cooked fresh, every day

    Breakfast, lunch and two snacks, made in-house each morning. Milk with lunch.

  • Real ingredients, small portions

    Whole grains, fruit and vegetables at every meal, and portions sized for the child in front of us.

  • Familiar food and new food

    Enough of what they already love that they eat, and enough of what they don't yet that they try.

  • Never a bargaining chip

    No child is made to finish a plate, and food is never used as a reward or a punishment.

Allergies are handled seriously here.

If your child has one, this is the part of the page that matters. Tell us at the tour and we will walk you through exactly what we do.

  • Written down before day one. Every allergy, intolerance and dietary restriction is recorded on enrollment and posted in the kitchen where it is cooked, not filed away in a folder.
  • Separated while it's cooked. Separate boards, utensils and prep space for an allergy meal, and it is plated first, before the allergen is anywhere near the counter.
  • Labeled at the table. An allergy plate is named and goes to one child. Nothing is shared off another child's plate, and that rule is enforced by an adult, not by a three-year-old's memory.
  • Nothing new without a parent's say-so. If we want to introduce a food, we ask you first. No surprises, no "we tried it and it was fine".
  • Birthday and treat drop-offs are allowed. You are welcome to bring something in for your child's birthday. Please check with us beforehand so we can work around every allergy in the room, and so nobody has to sit the party out.

Please tell us everything, even the mild ones. A stomach ache we could have avoided still ruins a child's afternoon, and knowing early is always easier than finding out late.

Want to know what's cooking this week, or whether we can work around something specific? Reach us at 425-428-9660 and ask. You'll get a straight answer from the person doing the cooking.
